steps: A charged particle in a uniform electric field E experiences force F=qE, causing linear motion if initial velocity u is parallel to E.
If u is perpendicular to E, the particle experiences constant acceleration perpendicular to u, resulting in parabolic motion.
A charged particle in a uniform magnetic field B experiences force F=q(v x B), which is zero if v is parallel to B, resulting in straight-line motion.
If u is perpendicular to B, the force F=qvB acts as a centripetal force, resulting in circular motion in a plane normal to B.
